t001_title: Neural Logic · AI colleagues that read what your company already holds
t003_h1: Hi, I'm Vera. I look after the AI colleagues that Neural Logic builds.
t004_p: Below is my colleague Frida, with four archives of one company open in front of her.
t007_p: One question. Sixteen thousand documents from four archives.
t008_p: Frida reads exactly as fast as you scroll. Stop, and she waits. Every document is connected to the case it belongs to; nothing is skipped in silence.
t011_p: In date order, quoted word for word, with the original one click away. And the one thing she could not find, said plainly.
t012_div: FridaFile reader
t022_h2: 16.863 documents in four archives. Nobody has time to read them all.
t023_p: Contracts, mails, invoices, protocols, scans. The answer to almost any question is in there somewhere. Finding it by hand takes hours, and nobody can say for certain what is missing.
t024_p: Demonstration on sample data. The archives and the case are invented; the mechanism is real.

t038_div: “…prices are fixed for twelve months from first delivery…”
t072_div: “…adjusted once a year by the producer price index…”
t075_div: Mail from Nordvik: “signed copy to follow”
t076_div: “…the countersigned amendment will follow by post this week…”
t083_div: “…Nordvik confirms the indexed price from January; the signed amendment is still outstanding…”
t117_div: A signed copy of the 2023 amendment.
t118_div: “The mail of 9 November 2023 promises it and the reminder of 18 June 2024 asks for it again. It is not in the contract folder and not in the mail archive. If it exists, it is not in the material I was given.”
t121_h2: Done in 4.2 seconds. By hand, in a real case: over an hour.
t122_p: 16.863 documents read, 27 connected to the case, the five that decide it quoted word for word, and one gap named instead of skipped. Sample data and an invented case; the mechanism is real.
t124_p: Frida, who reads your documents, is chosen for where she processes: a European model, Mistral, run in Europe under a European contract. Your documents do not leave that boundary.
t125_p: I never see a document or a name. I see the shape of the work: what kind of question, how many documents, which word was missing. So I can be chosen for how well I think: today that is Claude, from Anthropic, and it runs outside Europe. It can, precisely because nothing of yours ever reaches me. Every night I read how Frida worked and improve her before the morning.
t126_p: One boundary, two roles, and a reason for each. It is the same for every colleague Neural Logic builds.
t128_h3: Reads how the work went. Never what it was about.
t129_p: Improves the colleague overnight: new vocabulary, better habits, fewer misses.

t147_li: FridaA document colleague for teams that manage assets and the paperwork around them: contracts, protocols, correspondence, invoices. The first contract is the proof on real cases.In preparation
t148_li: VeraFrida's supervisor. Reads how the work went each night, never a document, never a name, and improves Frida before morning. The same role will stand behind every colleague we ship.In preparation
t149_li: PiaA catalogue colleague for web shops that live off supplier data. Every day she reads the supplier's feed, keeps the shop's products true to it, and reports what changed and what she could not resolve. Running daily on a related shop of our own.Live, daily
t150_li: NextA working colleague built on a prospect's own case within days, so the decision is made on evidence rather than slides. And Pia for shops that are not our own.Testing on ourselves
t152_p: Any business whose knowledge sits in files nobody has time to read. The documents differ; the mechanism is the same.
t153_p: And whatever you decide about a colleague, the first phase leaves you with files a machine can read: work every company will have to do before long.
